subject: Human Evolution
title: Trapping and Fishing
description: A micro-lesson that makes Trapping and Fishing usable.

hook.text: Not all ice age food came from dramatic hunts. Quiet traps and weirs worked while the hunter slept.

buildup.text: Pit traps, snares, and fish weirs appear in the archaeological record from at least 20,000 years ago.

discovery.text: Traps are force multipliers: one person sets them, and prey catches itself over hours or days.

twist.text: Fish bones at ice age sites show systematic river exploitation—not occasional, but seasonal harvesting.

climax.text: Trapping and fishing provided steady, low-risk calories that supplemented high-risk megafauna hunts.

punchline.text: The smartest hunters let the trap do the work.

quiz.question: Why were traps important in ice age subsistence?
options: They provided steady, low-risk calories alongside hunting
